clue.text: The relative, in short, defended in argument

parts.note: taken as written
a sister, the relative, is shortened to the familiar sis

explanation.surface: A family member, put briefly, was stood up for during a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctoral candidate must defend a dissertation or proposition in front of examiners, so it is a position upheld by reasoning.

clue.text: Building part of school

explanation.surface: A plain description of a school block.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a building, and British schools divide pupils into competing groups with that name for sport and pastoral care.

clue.text: Disregardin' in South America an' Italian girl

indicators.note: the dropped-g word sits inside the abbreviation for the continent

parts.note: disregarding means ignoring, here with its final g dropped to give ignorin'

explanation.surface: A drawling traveller in South America pays no attention to a young woman from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes are the clue's signal that letters go missing: ignorin' is ignoring without the G. The 'an'' is a dialect link word for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian title for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Louis XIV almost got taken on board

indicators.note: almost means the nickname is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Louis XIV of France was known as the Sun King

explanation.surface: The French monarch was nearly absorbed by a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken on board' suggests a ship, but it means understood: something that has been grasped has finally penetrated the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: When an idea has been absorbed and understood, people say it has finally penetrated.

clue.text: Stole various notes (but not F)

explanation.surface: A thief took an assortment of banknotes, leaving out one kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like money, but they are the letter names of musical notes, A to G; the brackets warn that F is the only note not used in the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage is old tailors' slang for cloth pilfered from a customer's material, hence a verb meaning to pinch.

clue.text: Border country for young pumpkin-eaters?

parts.note: a stretch of shoreline in India, recalled from Edward Lear's nonsense poem about a place where the early pumpkins blow

explanation.surface: A question about where children who devour pumpkins might live.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear's 'The Courtship of the Yonghy-Bonghy-Bò' opens 'On the Coast of Coromandel, where the early pumpkins blow'; 'young' pumpkins are those early ones, and 'border country' is a coast, the edge of land.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the south-eastern shoreline of India, and land at the sea's edge is the border of a country.

clue.text: But killers aren't charged here in Birmingham

definitions.text: But killers aren't charged here in Birmingham

parts.words: But killers aren't charged here in Birmingham
parts.note: in a Spanish arena it is the beasts that charge, not the matadors who kill them; in Birmingham the name belongs to a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A remark that murderers escape prosecution in a particular English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' reads as a legal accusation but means rushed at by an animal; in Birmingham, England's second city, the name is that of its central market and shopping area.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the arena for Spanish bullfights and also the name of Birmingham's famous shopping district.

clue.text: Had new commander — not general

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the first word are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A unit got a fresh commanding officer who was not of general rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like the army rank, but 'not general' is the definition: something improvised for one particular case.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes something arranged for a specific purpose only, rather than as a broad rule.

clue.text: Remarkable event such as eating forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: Biblical Eden: tasting the apple was quite a revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: A startling revelation is called this, and in Genesis eating the fruit literally made Adam and Eve's eyes open.

clue.text: Strategically excel, in particular? No, no!

parts.note: the opposite of in is out, which 'No' asks for
the opposite of particular is general, which the second 'no' asks for

explanation.surface: An exasperated correction: excelling in a specific way is denied twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'No' negates one word of 'in particular': in becomes OUT and particular becomes GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent through superior military tactics or leadership is to excel at strategy.

clue.text: Crust of bread — one of a pair waiter has to cool

definitions.text: one of a pair waiter has to cool

explanation.surface: Restaurant scene: a server waiting with bread while kept hanging about.
explanation.definitionFit: The end crust of a loaf has this name, and someone kept waiting is said to cool both of these feet parts.

clue.text: Male academic is getting married in pursuit of pleasure

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A male lecturer gets wed in search of enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosophy that seeking enjoyment is the highest good is named after the Greek for delight.

clue.text: Add 8 to revised price for prescription

indicators.note: add something to a word means it is attached after it, so the clue's order is turned round
revised means the five letters of the cost word are rearranged

parts.note: a cross-reference to 8 down, whose solution read cryptically is the opener of 'eye', the letter E

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a number on top of an updated cost.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' is a cross-reference: 8 down, read literally, is the opener of 'eye', which is the letter E. 'Revised' rearranges price, and 'Add ... to' puts the E after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors' prescriptions once began with the Latin for 'take', and the word long meant a medical formula.

clue.text: Some tribal islanders found here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain tribespeople live on this island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island is a place where islanders are, so it fits 'here' in the clue's sentence.

clue.text: To alter is unusual for a philosopher

indicators.note: unusual signals the three words are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Changing things would be out of character for a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek pupil of Plato is among the most famous ancient thinkers.

clue.text: It happens to be an anticlimax nobody expresses

definitions.text: It happens to be an anticlimax

parts.note: nobody means none, not a single person
to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: Something turns out a letdown, and no one says so.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: such a thing does in fact happen, it is simply disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: A much-anticipated occasion that proves dull or insignificant is a letdown.

clue.text: Police division putting deputies over prison, say

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: vices are deputies, as in vice-chairmen
quad is slang for a prison, a variant of quod

explanation.surface: Police place assistants in charge of a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the police unit dealing with gambling, prostitution and drugs.

clue.text: Write brief quotation on defense HQ

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a short familiar quotation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jot down a short quote about the military headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building in Virginia is the US Department of Defense headquarters.

clue.text: Motorway sections heading east of Italian city

indicators.note: the road sections lead or head the compass letter, coming before it

parts.note: Britain's first motorway, the M1, is often written MI in crosswords
lanes are the divisions of a road

explanation.surface: Stretches of highway lead eastward from a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things from Milan, as in a breaded veal cutlet.

clue.text: Preserve priest suffering acute lack

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a serious shortage tries to keep things going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acute' looks like severe, but it is the accent: a French parish priest without the acute accent on his final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve meat or fish is to salt or smoke it, and a French parish priest is a curé, here missing its accent.

clue.text: Novel hero lacking any plan

explanation.surface: A fictional protagonist who has no strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderick, title character of Smollett's eighteenth-century novel, bears this surname, which also means haphazard.

clue.text: Where snob went to work, finally

explanation.surface: A social climber got a job after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snob' is an old word for a cobbler, who works at a last, the foot-shaped block for making shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler works with a foot-shaped block, and the phrase also means in the end, after delay.

clue.text: A change of mind for management group

indicators.note: change of tells us the letters of the following word are altered in order

explanation.surface: Bosses have a rethink.
explanation.definitionFit: The administration, a firm's managing staff, is often shortened this way.

clue.text: Sort that could be elegant if accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the two-letter word is taken inside the other

parts.note: classy means elegant, stylish

explanation.surface: A kind of thing that might be stylish if welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange them into groups or categories.

clue.text: Disastrous way of addressing Capone?

explanation.surface: A question about greeting the gangster, with dire results.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone's first name is Al, so a teasing nickname for him splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly or ruinous outcomes are disastrous, and the phrase splits into a teasing nickname for the gangster Al Capone.

clue.text: Leaves supporter in front of ship

explanation.surface: Someone who walks out with a backer at the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb, departs, but is foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's stalk holds up its foliage, and the timber at a vessel's bow has this name, as in 'from stem to stern'.

clue.text: A female relative briefly frightens others

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother
to daunt is to intimidate or frighten

explanation.surface: Granny scares everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: these are further female relatives beyond the grandmother just named.
explanation.definitionFit: Great-aunts are additional kinswomen, the sisters of one's grandparents, beyond the nearer family.

clue.text: Fishing gear gets river clear

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris
net means clear, as profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Tackle for anglers arrives from a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large vertical net drawn round a shoal of fish.

clue.text: Standardized unit in game held back by me

indicators.note: held by me puts the reversed board game between the two letters of me

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back says the game's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Ludo is a British board game played with dice and counters

explanation.surface: A standard part in a match kept back by the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contained component of standard size used in building or teaching courses.
